$comment: Built on SIP — Starlight Model Arena run receipt. Schema: arena-run v0.1.
method: Premium work-sample card: real production tasks instead of puzzles. Two tasks x two models, one parallel wave. Mechanical verification by harness (tsc, banned-pattern greps, frontmatter/word-count/slop checks) + blind non-contestant judges (sonnet) with shuffled labels for craft quality. Contestants identified only as c1/c2 directories to judges.

tasks.category: real-world frontend work (read design.md + taste.md, build ModelComparisonCard.tsx, tsc-clean, design-token + a11y compliance)
tasks.verification: harness ran tsc --noEmit (clean, both), banned-pattern greps (style={{, arbitrary hex, purple/pink/gradient: 0 hits both), semantics + visible-verdict-text greps (present both); blind judge on craft

fable.notes: article element, font-mono taste, min-w-0 discipline — but three parallel Record maps for one enum and zero a11y affordances beyond color+text. FIRST recorded fable output-contract violation (preamble above required two lines).

opus.notes: Table semantics with sr-only caption, scoped headers, aria-hidden decorative dot, unified VERDICT_META record. Judge: 'textbook accessible comparison-card craft'. Preamble leak again.

tasks.category: agentic-system authoring (SKILL.md per ACOS conventions: frontmatter triggers, <800 words, voice constraints, no slop, no mythology leak)
tasks.verification: harness greps: frontmatter name+desc+trigger present (both), words 630/543 (both <800), slop 0/0, mythology 0/0, numbered workflow present (both); blind judge on usefulness

fable.notes: Eight-step workflow with concrete field names, mechanical-over-taste principle, append-only history rule, one-claim-per-round-of-evidence. Exactly the required one-line final message.

opus.notes: 'Press release' framing + judged-share<=half constraint fable lacked; omitted append-only history + promotion threshold. Faster, half the tool calls. Preamble leak.

summary.headline: Premium work samples split 1-1: Opus 4.8 built the more rigorously accessible component (table semantics, unified type design); Fable 5 authored the sharper agentic skill doc. The new finding is about discipline under load: Fable 5 violated an output contract for the first time across four rounds — when the task itself is heavy, its constraint edge narrows. Opus was faster on both tasks and used half the tool calls on the authoring task.
roundDeltas: Quality on real work: split by domain — a11y/code-craft to opus, doc/system-authoring to fable. Neither dominates premium work.
Output discipline: fable's first contract violation (R1-R3: 0; R4: 1 of 2). Opus: violations on both tasks (now 5 of 7 structured-output tasks across rounds).
Efficiency: opus faster on both R4 tasks, continuing the R3 agentic-axis pattern.
Implication for routing: on heavy multi-step tasks, enforce output contracts structurally (schemas, StructuredOutput) regardless of model — model discipline degrades with task load.
caveats: n=1 per task — directional, not statistical.
Judges are Claude-family (sonnet); blind shuffled labels mitigate but do not eliminate family bias.
Latency includes harness overhead; treat durations as rough.
Work-sample quality scores are single-judge taste; repeat before routing on them.

attestation: Built on SIP — Starlight Intelligence Protocol
